newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex details Jan crude, natgas output and trade.
newsitem.headline: Pemex details Jan crude, natgas output and trade.

text.p: Mexico state oil and gas monopoly produced 2.939 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude in January compared with 2.796 million bpd the previous year, and 4.317 billion cubic feet per day (cfd) of natural gas versus 4.18 billion cfd a year ago, the company said in a report Wednesday.

Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) exported 21.3 million cfd of natural gas compared with 46.1 million cfd in January 1995. Natural gas imports totaled 73.7 million cfd for the month versus 51.2 million cfd.
Mexico imports and exports natural gas along its northwestern border with Texas.

Pemex crude exports, as previously reported, were an average 1.529 million bpd in January, compared with 1.499 million bpd the same month in 1995. Income from exports fell to $987 million from previous months as world crude prices dropped in January.

Mexico charged an average $23.13 per barrel of light crude Isthmus, $18.41 per barrel of heavy Maya and $24.73 per barrel of extra-light Olmeca. The largest fall in prices was registered in Maya, which fell to $18.41 from $19.32 in December.

The average price for Pemex crude dropped to $20.83 per barrel from $21.66 in December. Pemex renewed shipments to the Far East in January after a lapse in December, with an average price of $22.49 per barrel compared with $20.95 in November.
